videos.title: Notes payable at present value
videos.take: A note with no or unreasonable interest is recorded at present value; the discount becomes interest expense

scenes.say: Bluestem buys a lot for its new plant. The seller accepts a $300,000 note due in three years, with no interest.
Nobody lends for free. A note with no stated interest has interest hidden in its face. Recording the land at $300,000 would overstate the land and understate interest expense.

scenes.heading: Imputing interest at 8%
rows: Face of note, due in 3 years
Present value: cost of the land
scenes.say: Bluestem's borrowing rate for similar notes is eight percent. The present value, $238,149, is the land's cost. The $61,851 discount will be recognized as interest over three years.

scenes.heading: Year 1 interest
scenes.say: Year-one interest is eight percent of $238,149, $19,052, added to the note's carrying amount. Year two's interest is eight percent of the new balance, and so on to $300,000.

sub: If the land's fair value is known,
scenes.say: If the land's fair value were reliably known, say from a recent appraisal, Bluestem would use it, and the implied rate would follow. When neither is clear, impute a rate the company would pay on similar debt.

scenes.q: Equipment bought for a $100,000 zero-interest note due in 2 years; imputed rate 10%. Equipment cost?
scenes.say: Quick check. Equipment is bought for a one hundred thousand dollar zero-interest note due in two years; imputed rate ten percent. Equipment cost? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Extinguishing debt early
videos.take: Gain or loss = carrying amount − reacquisition price, reported in income

scenes.say: Two years after issuing its discount bonds, rates have dropped. Bluestem calls the bonds at 102.

scenes.heading: Carrying amount after 4 periods
scenes.say: After four semiannual periods of effective-interest amortization, the bonds' carrying amount has grown from $1,837,774 to $1,895,147.

scenes.heading: Calling the bonds
scenes.say: Calling at a hundred and two costs $2,040,000. The difference from the carrying amount, $144,853, is a loss on extinguishment of debt.

scenes.heading: The entry
scenes.say: Bluestem removes the bonds at carrying amount, pays $2,040,000, and records the loss in income from continuing operations. Any unamortized issuance costs would also be written off as part of the loss.

sub: Refinancing at a lower rate can
scenes.say: Why take a loss? Because refinancing at a much lower rate can save more in future interest than the call premium costs. The loss is the price of that saving.

scenes.q: Bonds with carrying amount $990,000 are retired for $975,000. Result?
scenes.say: Quick check. Bonds with carrying amount nine ninety thousand are retired for nine seventy-five thousand. Result? Pause and pick.

videos.title: The fair value option
videos.take: Companies may measure debt at fair value; changes due to own credit risk go to OCI

scenes.say: GAAP lets companies choose to measure some financial liabilities at fair value instead of amortized cost.
The fair value option is an election, made instrument by instrument when the debt is issued, and it's irrevocable. Changes in fair value are then recognized each period.

scenes.heading: If Bluestem had elected it
scenes.say: Suppose Bluestem elected the fair value option. At the end of 2028, the bonds' amortized cost is $1,865,336, but market rates have risen and their fair value is $1,820,000. The liability falls by $45,336.

scenes.heading: Where the change goes
scenes.say: The part of the change caused by general interest rates goes to net income. The part caused by Bluestem's own credit getting worse goes to other comprehensive income, so a company doesn't report profit just because it became riskier.
Companies elect it mainly to reduce volatility caused by measuring related assets at fair value and liabilities at cost. Most companies don't use it for their own bonds.

scenes.q: Under the fair value option, a decline in a liability's fair value caused by the company's worsening credit is reported in:
scenes.say: Quick check. Under the fair value option, a decline in a liability's fair value caused by the company's worsening credit goes where? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Troubled debt settlements
videos.take: A debtor settling debt with assets recognizes a gain on disposal and a gain on settlement

scenes.say: One of Bluestem's dealers, Lakes Paddle Co., is in trouble. It owes its bank $500,000 and can't pay.

sub: Creditor grants a concession to a
scenes.say: A troubled debt restructuring happens when a creditor, for economic or legal reasons related to the debtor's financial difficulties, grants a concession it wouldn't otherwise consider.

scenes.heading: Settlement with land
scenes.say: Lakes settles its $500,000 loan by giving the bank land worth $380,000, with a book value of $300,000. It records two gains: $80,000 on disposing of the land, and $120,000 on settling the debt for less than owed.

sub: Lower rate, longer term, reduced principal:
gain only if future cash < carrying amount
scenes.say: If instead the bank modifies the terms, lowering the rate or extending the term, the debtor recognizes a gain only if total future cash payments, undiscounted, are less than the carrying amount.

sub: As a creditor, it would test its
scenes.say: If Lakes owed Bluestem instead, Bluestem would treat it as a creditor and measure expected credit losses under CECL, from Intermediate One.

scenes.q: Debt $200,000 settled with equipment: fair value $150,000, book value $170,000. Gain on settlement?
scenes.say: Quick check. Debt of two hundred thousand is settled with equipment worth one fifty thousand, book value one seventy thousand. Gain on settlement? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, $50,000. There's also a $20,000 loss on disposal.

videos.title: Off-balance-sheet financing
videos.take: Companies try to keep debt off the balance sheet; standards have closed many routes, so read the notes

scenes.say: Bluestem's founder asks: can we borrow without the debt showing up?
Off-balance-sheet financing is an attempt to borrow money without recording the obligation, keeping debt ratios and covenants looking better.

scenes.heading: Common forms
scenes.say: Common forms include non-consolidated entities and joint ventures; take-or-pay contracts that commit the company to buy output; and receivables sold with recourse. Operating leases were the biggest until the lease standard put them on the balance sheet.

Standards have closed many routes: variable interest entities must be consolidated, leases are recognized, and commitments must be disclosed. So the answer to the founder is mostly no, and trying would worry lenders.
Analysts read the notes on commitments, guarantees and unconsolidated entities to find obligations that aren't in the liability totals.

scenes.q: Which change brought most leases onto the balance sheet?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which change brought most leases onto the balance sheet? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Presenting and analyzing long-term debt
videos.take: Disclose maturities, rates, covenants and fair values; debt to assets and times interest earned measure risk

scenes.say: Bluestem's lenders and new bondholders watch two numbers closely.

scenes.heading: Required disclosures
items: Maturities for each of the next 5 years
scenes.say: Notes disclose aggregate maturities for each of the next five years, interest rates and terms, assets pledged as collateral, covenants and any violations, and the fair value of the debt.

scenes.heading: Bluestem, 2028
scenes.say: After the bonds and the Northwind purchase, Bluestem's total liabilities are $3.6 million and total assets $7.2 million: debt to assets of fifty percent, up from about thirty-nine percent.

scenes.heading: Times interest earned
scenes.say: Times interest earned is earnings before interest and taxes over interest expense: $1.28 million over $180,000, seven point one times. Bluestem earns its interest seven times over, a comfortable cushion.
Covenants are often written in these terms. A breach can make the debt callable at once, which would also make it a current liability.

scenes.q: Income before tax $600,000; interest expense $150,000. Times interest earned?
scenes.say: Quick check. Income before tax six hundred thousand; interest expense one fifty thousand. Times interest earned? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, five times: seven fifty over one fifty.
